rationale: Psalm 110:4 (BSB) is the only verse outside Genesis 14 in the Old Testament where the name appears: 'You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek' (checked by a full scan of this app's BSB text, which finds the name only at Genesis 14:18, 14:20, Psalm 110:4, and eleven verses of Hebrews). Named commentators read the psalm as drawing on Genesis 14: Matthew Poole says the priest-word 'signifies a priest in Genesis 14:18, from whence this expression is borrowed,' and Ellicott says the psalmist had 'to go back to Melchizedek, in whom history recognised this sanctioned and formal union (Genesis 14:18)' of king and priest. Graded strong rather than explicit for two textual reasons: the psalm gives no narrative detail from Genesis 14 (no Abram, no bread and wine, no tithe), and the Hebrew phrase can be read as a title rather than a name -- the Talmud's own rendering at Nedarim 32b (William Davidson Edition) translates the clause 'because you are a king of righteousness [al divrati malki tzedek]' before applying it to Melchizedek anyway. The person-reference is the overwhelmingly common reading, which is why the grade is strong and not plausible.
